items.title: Milt Hinton interviewed by Joe Williams, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: That’s what we tried to do, the three of us, Hank Jones, Barry Galbraith, Osie Johnson and myself. We tried to play for you what you, it’s your date, we’ve got to make you sound good.

ctx.x: I tell people I say like 50 years and for you it’s even longer, that your association has been with musicians.

That’s right. I can’t tell you how proud I feel and how grateful. I remember what really made me feel so great, after knowing you all these years, and I was at Carnegie Hall, and I was in a band, and man I felt so good, I’d say, I could remember the time Joe would be there and would say we’re going to play this tune before the singer come out to sing, and I was so glad to be here, for the singer. It was beautiful.
Yeah, that was quite a thing. George Wein made that thing possible. He told me he said, “It’s time for you to produce your own show.” I said, “Oh?” I said, “Okay.” And of © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-

items.title: Hinton Milt — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Joe Williams was the vocalist... and I was doing fairly well on bass, and we played Baker‟s Casino and all the Saturday night things and played the Warrick Hall

ctx.x: So that was a lot work then for people.

A lot of work. See everybody was… reminds me, all blacks from the south… that‟s the reason you see so many… I know just from my experience of my school days, the guys that I came up with, Joe Williams and all, they came from Alabama. Our folks were coming from Mississippi. Tennessee people were coming to Chicago, once they were listening to these ministers and things and getting their young people out. And they all congregated in Chicago because there was lots of work. There was also a lot of good decent housing…
You can afford it, that‟s right.

items.title: Joe Williams interviewed by Leslie Gourse, New York City, New York, March 9, 1996
items.q: Milt Hinton, Kenny Burrell, oh boy, Romeo Penque, Harold Lookofsky.

ctx.x: Harry “Sweets” Edison, and I like that Bohanon, the trombonist you worked with, and so many of them. I mean I love them. Jimmy Jones and everyone.
Yup, yup, yup, yup, yup. Hank Jones, Jimmy Jones, Osie Johnson, Milt Hinton, Kenny Burrell, oh boy, Romeo Penque, Harold Lookofsky. Really all these wonderful — Zoot Sims, Frank Foster, and —
And the Jones-Lewis band. The Thad Jones-Mel Lewis band.
